summary: Russian forces launched a massive strike after Ukraine’s Independence Day, prompting President Zelensky to warn civilians. Ukrainian air defenses shot down 9 aviation bombs and 811 UAVs, showing active counter‑air operations. Russian attacks on fuel infrastructure, including gas stations in Zaporizhzhia and Kharkiv, and tankers in the Azov Sea, have caused casualties and disrupted logistics.
key_points: Russian forces launched a massive strike after Ukraine’s Independence Day, prompting President Zelensky to warn civilians. (Source: UkraineNow/82434)
Ukrainian air defenses shot down 9 aviation bombs and 811 UAVs, indicating active counter‑air capabilities. (Source: tass_agency/384002)
Russian attacks on gas stations in Zaporizhzhia injured five civilians, while a separate strike on a Kharkiv gas station was documented. (Source: UkraineNow/82446, eRadarrua/99959)
Two Russian tankers in the Azov Sea, each carrying 7000 tons of fuel, were attacked, disrupting logistics to annexed Crimea. (Source: UkraineNow/82448)
Reactive UAVs were observed in Sumy from the northwest and in Dnipropetrovsk near N. Yuriyivka heading west, indicating continued Russian aerial harassment. (Source: kpszsu/67503, kpszsu/67561)

Ukrainian authorities moved high school students from nine Kharkiv communities to military exercises and sent university students from Kharkiv and Zaporizhzhia to special sabotage training courses. (Source: tass_agency/384022)
Russian UAV activity included Shahed drones from Bryansk and Millerovo, with about 10 groups observed, increasing pressure on Ukrainian rear areas. (Source: eRadarrua/99926)
An air alert was issued in Kyiv at 08:14 on 06.07.2026, reflecting heightened threat perception. (Source: eRadarrua/99910)

sections.threat_assessment: Russian tactical aviation activity in multiple directions and persistent UAV harassment of Ukrainian rear areas increase the risk of escalation. The targeting of fuel infrastructure, including gas stations and tankers, threatens supply lines and civilian safety. Ukrainian air defenses have demonstrated capacity to shoot down numerous bombs and UAVs, but continued Russian pressure may strain resources and force a shift in operational tempo.
sections.regional_response: Ukrainian officials have requested new funding for drone production, citing European Commission support. US intelligence reportedly provides optimal routes for Ukrainian drones to bypass Russian air defenses, enabling strikes on Russian refineries. NATO’s Air Defence Coalition is engaged in procurement of Patriot, IRIS‑T, and NASAMS missiles, though details remain limited.
sections.intelligence_notes: US intelligence is reportedly guiding Ukrainian forces on routes to avoid Russian air defenses, facilitating strikes on Russian oil refineries. According to a Financial Times report, Ukrainian drones have hit Russian refineries at least 194 times since early 2026, 11 times more than the previous year. These operations rely on real‑time intelligence and coordination with allied partners.
